# Tools

These tools are separate from project editors. Open the named dialogs from
the **Tools** menu; open dockable panels from **Window** or the workbench.

## Code Repository

**Tools → Code Repository Editor** opens a personal tree of code groups and
snippets. Add a group or snippet from the tree's context menu, rename it in
the tree, and edit a selected snippet in the code area. **Save** applies
changes. **Import…** and **Export…** exchange the repository with Java Blue
XML. Blue stores the repository with its application data, not in the open
`.blue` project, so use **Export…** when you need a portable copy. In a
Csound editor, use its context menu to insert a snippet or add selected text
to the repository. The repository is separate from the project's orchestra
and UDO list.

## Effects Library

**Tools → Effects Library** opens reusable mixer effects. Organize effects
in folders, import effect XML with the Libraries actions menu, and
double-click an effect to edit it. Add a library effect to a mixer chain
from the mixer or by dragging it from Libraries. See
[Mixer](mixer.qmd) for routing, chain order, sends, and channel settings.

## FTable Converter

**Tools → FTable Converter** accepts Csound `f` statements in its upper
editor. Click **Convert to FTGEN** and copy the output from the lower
editor into orchestra code. The converter changes numbered score tables
into `ftgen` assignments; inspect and name the generated `gi_` variables
before using them. It does not insert its output into the project.

## Csound configuration editor

**Tools → .csound7rc Editor** edits the configuration file shown by the
dialog's path label. **Save** writes the text; **Cancel** closes without
writing. By default, Blue opens `.csound7rc` in your home directory. If
`CSOUNDRC` is set, Blue opens that path instead. Check the selected file
and Csound flags before saving. The older manual described a `.csoundrc`
editor; Blue 3's menu and dialog use `.csound7rc`.

## SoundFont Viewer

Open **Window → Properties → SoundFont Viewer**, or double-click an `.sf2`
file in the File Manager. The viewer lists the SoundFont's instruments and
presets after Blue's managed Csound runtime inspects the file. This is an
inspection tool; selecting a preset here does not add it to an instrument
or Score automatically.

## Code editors and consoles

Csound text editors appear in **Global Orchestra**, **Tables**, **UDOs**,
instrument editors, and other panels. Their context menu offers Csound
opcode help and Code Repository actions where appropriate. The older
manual's NetBeans editor preferences and shortcuts do not describe this
workbench.

Open **Python Console** from **Window → REPL → Python Console** for the
Java-backed Jython session used by supported Python content. **JavaScript
Console** and **Clojure REPL** are separate panels in the same submenu. A
Python or JavaScript console is useful for diagnosis, but the project code
still belongs in the relevant instrument, SoundObject, or processor editor.

## Blue Share

**Tools → Blue Share** opens the community sharing dialog with three resource
groups: **Instruments**, **Effects**, and **SoundObjects**. Each group provides
three workflows via dedicated tabs: **Import**, **Export**, and **Manage**.

### Browsing and Importing

Public browsing and importing work anonymously without signing in:

- **Categories and Latest**: Browse remote categories in the left panel or click
  **Latest Submissions** to view the ten most recent additions of that kind.
- **Details**: Selecting an item displays its title, author, publication date,
  category, type, and author's description.
- **Importing**: Clicking **Import to Library** downloads and validates the complete
  standalone XML, saving an independent copy into your User Library under
  `Imported Instruments`, `Imported Effects`, or `Imported SoundObjects`.
  Imported resources survive restart and do not alter the open project or its
  history. You can later drag or insert them into your project arrangement,
  mixer, or score as normal.
- **Content Limits**: Unsupported or invalid serialized content is rejected
  atomically with explanatory diagnostics. Missing opcodes or external plugins
  do not block library storage, but runtime dependencies must be satisfied when
  rendering in Csound.

### Exporting and Publishing

Sharing your own resources requires signing in with your Blue Share account:

- **Source Selection**: Choose any supported item from your local User Library.
  The resource name, type, and embedded comments are read from your local library.
- **Destination and Description**: Select a valid destination category and enter
  an optional public description (up to 64 KiB). Editing the public description
  does not mutate your local library item. Your reviewed source, category, and exact
  description remain available after sign-out or session expiry; select the source
  again to review it for the new session. **Reset export** clears the draft.
- **Publishing**: Click **Publish to Blue Share** to submit. The source XML (up to
  2 MiB) is validated before upload. Confirmed submissions appear immediately in
  public listings and in your Manage tab.
- **Uncertain Outcomes**: If a network timeout occurs while publishing, Blue
  Share retains your draft and flags the outcome as uncertain. Check your
  submissions in the Manage tab before retrying to prevent duplicate publications.
  The recovery stays with its original resource group when you navigate elsewhere.
  After refreshing all submissions, **Restore submitted draft for review** brings
  back the exact submitted fields without publishing again; select the source again
  before deciding whether to retry.

### Managing Submissions

The **Manage** tab lets signed-in users review and remove their submissions:

- **Fetch Submissions**: Clicking **Fetch submissions** lists all resources of the active kind published by
  your account. Use **Load more** to page through older submissions.
- **Removal**: Selecting an owned item enables the **Remove Submission** button.
  A confirmation dialog names the selected item and defaults focus to **Cancel**.
  Confirming removal deletes the item from public availability on the server.
- **Local Copy Safety**: Remote removal never deletes or modifies local copies
  already imported into your User Library or referenced in your projects.
- **Uncertain Removal**: If deletion confirmation times out, refresh your
  submissions before attempting to remove again.

### Accounts and Recovery

- **Opening and Timeouts**: The dialog shows progress while opening and offers
  **Retry opening** if initialization fails. Local library requests time out after
  30 seconds. A timed-out import may still finish; check the User Library before
  trying another import of the same resource.
- **Session Security**: Sign-in requires your email address and password. Account
  sessions normally last only for the running application process. Check **Stay
  signed in on this computer** when signing in to keep the session for up to seven
  days, including after restarting Blue. The checkbox is off by default; using Blue
  does not extend the seven days. Blue saves only OS-protected session proof, never
  your password, and verifies it with the server when Blue Share next opens.
  Signing out clears saved sign-in even when offline; Blue reports if local cleanup
  or remote revocation could not be confirmed. If protected storage is unavailable,
  sign-in still works for the current process and Blue explains that it cannot
  remember the session. Project files, libraries and logs never contain credentials.
  Public browsing and importing remain available while saved sign-in is checked.
  If a saved session cannot be verified temporarily, use **Retry verification**,
  **Forget saved sign-in** (also available offline), or sign in again. Account
  operations recover within 30 seconds; a timeout does not confirm that saved
  proof was deleted or the remote session revoked. Blue shows any unconfirmed
  cleanup so you can try again. Expired or revoked sessions require a new sign-in.
- **Account Management**: Use the dialog's **Create an account** and **Forgot
  password?** links to open the registration and password reset pages in your
  external web browser.

## Historical tools

The old **Scanned Synthesis Matrix Editor** and **Manage Tools** menu from
Java Blue are absent from the current Tools menu. Their original descriptions
remain in the [Blue 2 source edition](https://github.com/kunstmusik/blue-manual/tree/7a92066a2aa8f0370026ba9527c158643c2935a1)
for historical reference.
